# TFHE-rs Encryption Benchmark

[Dylan Gresham](https://github.com/Dylan-Gresham)

This README was generated by Claude from the source code in this repository. Claude Sonnet 5 Medium was also used in the source code for debugging and design assistance.*

## Overview

A small Rust benchmark that measures how long it takes to homomorphically encrypt image-sized data with [TFHE-rs](https://github.com/zama-ai/tfhe-rs), comparing two encryption strategies across single-threaded and multi-threaded (Rayon) execution.

## What it measures

The benchmark treats a 4K grayscale image (3840 × 2160 = 8,294,400 byte values) as the target workload and times four encryption strategies:

| Section |                Strategy                |     Threading    |
|:-------:|:--------------------------------------:|:----------------:|
|    1a   | Naive per-value `ClientKey` encryption |  Single-threaded |
|    1b   | Batched `CompactPublicKey` encryption  |  Single-threaded |
|    2a   | Naive per-value `ClientKey` encryption | Parallel (Rayon) |
|    2b   | Batched `CompactPublicKey` encryption  | Parallel (Rayon) |

For each section it reports total elapsed time, effective per-value wall-clock time, and an extrapolated time for a full 4K image. Section 2 also reports the speedup versus its single-threaded counterpart.

## Memory-safe streaming

Materializing ciphertexts for all 8.3M values of a full 4K image at once will exhaust memory on most machines and get the process killed (SIGKILL) with no error message. To avoid this, the benchmark processes data in fixed-size batches and drops each batch's ciphertexts before generating the next one, so peak memory stays bounded to roughly one batch's worth of ciphertexts rather than the whole image.

This is controlled by two constants at the top of `main.rs`:

```rust
const FULL_IMAGE: bool = true;     // `true`: stream the full 8.3M-value image
                                   // `false`: run a single in-memory sample
const SAMPLE_SIZE: usize = 5_000;  // batch size when `FULL_IMAGE` is `true`,
                                   // or sample size when `FULL_IMAGE` is `false`
```

- **`FULL_IMAGE = true`** --- streams through the full image in batches of `SAMPLE_SIZE` values, reporting progress roughly every 10%. Reported timings are real measurements across the whole image, not an extrapolation.
- **`FULL_IMAGE = false`** --- encrypts a single in-memory batch of `SAMPLE_SIZE` values and extrapolates the full-image time from that sample. Useful for quick iteration without waiting for a full run.

Increasing `SAMPLE_SIZE` reduces loop overhead (fewer batches) at the cost of higher peak memory; decreasing it does the opposite. Tune it based on the available RAM on your machine.

## Requirements

- Rust (stable toolchain, edition compatible with the crates below)
- Dependencies (declared in `Cargo.toml`):
  - [`tfhe`](https://crates.io/crates/tfhe) --- homomorphic encryption
  - [`rayon`](https://crates.io/crates/rayon) --- data parallelism
  - [`rand`](https://crates.io/crates/rand) --- random value generation

## Running

```bash
cargo run --release
```

Key generation happens once at startup and can take a few seconds. With `FULL_IMAGE = true`, expect the full run to take a while, especially in debug mode---the naive per-value `ClientKey` path in particular is significantly slower than the batched `CompactPublicKey` path.

## Interpreting the output

- **Effective per-value wall-clock time** --- average time per encrypted value, useful for comparing strategies independent of batch/sample size.
- **Extrapolated to a full 4K RGB image** --- projected time to encrypt `IMAGE_WIDTH * IMAGE_HEIGHT * CHANNELS` values. When `FULL_IMAGE = true` this is effectively the real measured time; when `false`, it's a projection from the sample.
- **Speedup vs. single-threaded** --- ratio of single-threaded to parallel time for the same strategy, printed after each Part 2 section.

## Notes

- `CHANNELS` is currently set to `1` (grayscale). Adjust `IMAGE_WIDTH`, `IMAGE_HEIGHT`, and `CHANNELS` to model a different image size or color format.
- Always benchmark in `--release` mode. Debug builds are useful for functional testing but are not representative of real encryption throughput.
- If the process is killed unexpectedly with no error output, check `dmesg`/`journalctl -k` for an OOM-killer entry and consider lowering `SAMPLE_SIZE`.
